steps.say: The policy line is ready to place; the number of days is yours.

input.title: Returns policy
input.question:
Which returns policy should the checkout show?
Customers see one line under the total, and support answers for whatever it says.
The last month had 212 returns. 140 came back inside two weeks, 61 inside a month, and 11 after that. Every late one was a gift bought early for a birthday or a wedding.
The warehouse can take up to 40 returns a day. At 30 days it would see about 9, and at 60 days about 11, with a peak of 35 in January.
Card refunds are free for 60 days. After that each one costs 0.30, and the customer's bank may refuse it, so store credit is the safe way to pay it back.
Two of the shops closest to ours show 30 days, one shows 14, and one shows a year but only for members.
Whatever you pick shows on the product page, the cart, the receipt and the order email. Orders already placed keep the policy they were bought under, and the wording is checked against the rules in every country we ship to before it goes live.
Changing it later means a new line on the receipt and a note to everyone with an open order, so it is better to settle it once.
input.pick: 30 days, what most shops nearby show

choices.label: 14 days, the least work for the warehouse
30 days, what most shops nearby show
60 days, while card refunds are still free
